svg.text: Most of the evidence lives past the first 1,024 tokens
Section-level oracle over the TREC CDS judged set: 2,161 (topic, relevant document) pairs, 90 topics, 2,095 documents. For each
pair the highest-scoring structural section is the 'evidence'; the panels describe where in the document it starts. Shading and
bars are 95% percentile-bootstrap intervals resampling topics, the clustering unit.
chunk sizes tested in the grid
token offset at which the evidence section starts (log scale)
share of (topic, document) pairs at or before
win rate among documents that have the section
The oracle is bge-reranker-v2-m3 — the same cross-encoder the production pipeline runs — so this measures where the evidence the reranker can find
lives, not ground truth. Strict definition throughout: the winning section BEGINS past the offset. Under the looser midpoint definition the past-1,024
share is 78.7%. Only 11.9% of wins (CI 10.6–13.5%) fall in abstract+intro and 3.0% in the lead unit, and in 88.0% of pairs some non-head section
strictly beats every abstract/intro section (median margin +0.163). Per-topic the past-1,024 rate ranges 20%–88% with 8 of 90 topics below 40%, so
this is a corpus-level statement, not a per-topic guarantee. 'other' is the largest winning class because it holds untitled body leads and
case-presentation sections — a real feature of a clinical corpus, not a parser artefact. In panel A the line is the pooled rate over all 2,161 pairs
and the band is the 95% interval from resampling the 90 topics; the pooled and topic-mean curves never differ by more than 0.004, and the pooled curve
